sources.content: Gorvel is an agent that collects host metrics and exposes them for scraping. Start it with gorvel run, and it serves metrics in Prometheus text format at /metrics on port 9310. By default it collects CPU, memory, disk and network metrics every 15 seconds. Add the flag --collectors=cpu,memory to collect only those two groups. The agent keeps the most recent sample of each metric in memory and stores nothing on disk.

To push metrics instead of waiting for scrapes, set push.url in /etc/gorvel/gorvel.toml. Gorvel then sends a batch every 30 seconds and gives up on a batch after 3 failed attempts. Every metric name starts with the prefix gorvel_. The agent adds a host label set to the machine's host name; change it with the host_label setting. Gorvel refuses to start if the config file contains an unknown key, and it prints the line number of that key.

claims.text: Every Gorvel metric name starts with the prefix gorvel_.
Gorvel serves metrics at /metrics on port 9310.
Gorvel refuses to start when its config file contains an unknown key.
Gorvel collects metrics every 60 seconds by default.
In push mode Gorvel sends a batch every 30 seconds.
The --collectors flag limits which metric groups Gorvel collects.
